subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to existing retention rules and report that in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and well-proven, but accepting retained session artifact deletion is a maintainer policy and upgrade-risk choice because related issues argue for broader archive preservation or renamed archive semantics.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention settings and current CLI proof.

options.title: Require broader store proof
options.body: Ask for a larger real-store or upgrade-style cleanup run before merge if retained artifact deletion needs more operational confidence.

options.title: Pause for artifact policy
options.body: Hold or close the PR if maintainers want the broader archive naming/no-delete policy settled before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention settings and current CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that define this operator-facing cleanup policy.
